NT$355 (based on unchanged 15x 2026E P/E). Unexciting earnings growth (-4%/+6% in 
2H26/2027) should limit re-rating potential. We reiterate Underperform as we see 
earnings downside risks caused by potentially weaker volumes and margins driven by
conservative customers’ orders and higher raw material costs.

items.story:
Feng Tay's (FT) valuation has fallen to a near trough 14x 2027E PE (1.6SD below average
since 2015), as inventory destocking and product restructuring at Nike drove a 
contraction in orders, while lower utilisation and production relocation weighed on 
OPM. FT's earnings troughed in February 2026 and improved sequentially for five 
months. However, the market has not responded positively due to weak confidence in 
Nike's order outlook. We expect revenue to stabilise and return to moderate growth, 
supported by Nike's launch of new training and basketball shoes, of which FT is a 
primary supplier, and our estimated double-digit order growth from Salomon. We think 
OPM should continue to recover as workers at the Southeast Asian plants gain 
experience. Our lower NT$90.00 price target implies 18x 2027E PE (-1SD) and a 26%
discount to Nike, both in line with the 11-year averages. We upgrade our rating to Buy 
from Neutral with 29% potential share price upside and a 5.0% dividend yield.

items.story:
We cut 2026-28E EPS by 9-18% to reflect 3Q26 preliminary sales, more conservative 
margin assumptions under material cost pressure, and higher share count (+1.3%) for 
new CB (total NT$300mn) and fund-raising plan (maximum 1.3mn shares). We cut PO to 
NT$2,245 (20x 2027E EPS) from NT$2,800 (was 22x) with valuation base unchanged but 
a lower P/E multiple. We lower P/E multiple to 20x (2SD above historical average) on 
industry-wise component tightness, which may partially cap CPU server market demand. 
In our view, Lotes’ near-term margin pressure has been fully reflected as its share price 
corrected 15% in 3Q26, vs. TAIEX +4%. We reiterate our Buy rating on Lotes as a clear 
CPU server beneficiary to capture still robust market demand,
with attractive valuation under 24%/36% sales/EPS CAGR in 2026-28.

買賣結論:We cut 2026-28E EPS by 9-18% to reflect 3Q26 preliminary sales, more conservative 
margin assumptions under material cost pressure, and higher share count (+1.3%) for 
new CB (total NT$300mn) and fund-raising plan (maximum 1.3mn shares). We cut PO to 
NT$2,245 (20x 2027E EPS) from NT$2,800 (was 22x) with valuation base unchanged but 
a lower P/E multiple. We lower P/E multiple to 20x (2SD above historical average) on 
industry-wise component tightness, which may partially cap CPU server market demand. 
In our view, Lotes’ near-term margin pressure has been fully reflected as its share price 
corrected 15% in 3Q26, vs. TAIEX +4%. We reiterate our Buy rating on Lotes as a clear 
CPU server beneficiary to capture still robust market demand,
with attractive valuation under 24%/36% sales/EPS CAGR in 2026-28.
